summary: container_vm_headroom_mb 3608->2351->1207 across 3 ticks is a transient ocr-bench container (2.476GiB/2.5GiB, unhealthy), NOT a service leak — mcp-server is 296MiB/3GiB. Guard the open pdf-extractor memory investigation against this contamination.
owner_hint: po to note against sys-20260825T142316-4385; no dev dispatch implied
detail:
MEASUREMENT (3 consecutive cowork ticks, pressure-state.json container_vm_headroom_mb):
  14:20:55Z -> 3608 MB
  14:35:14Z -> 2351 MB  (-1257)
  14:48:56Z -> 1207 MB  (-1144)
Monotone, ~1200 MB/tick. On n=1 I declined to file; on n=3 I probed docker before escalating.

ROOT CAUSE — transient peer benchmark, NOT a service leak:
  docker stats 14:50Z:
    ocr-bench-paddleocr-run2   2.476GiB / 2.5GiB   99.05%   (Up 7 min, UNHEALTHY)
    pdf-extractor-1            1.632GiB / 2.5GiB   65.27%
    rag-service-1              1.224GiB / 2GiB     61.20%
    mcp-server-1               296.4MiB / 3GiB      9.65%   <-- gateway is FINE
Correlates with two untracked peer files seen in git status at 14:35Z:
  scripts/audits/ocr-backend-bench.sh, scripts/audits/ocr_bench_inner.py
Container is named run2, so a run1 preceded it; run2 started ~14:42Z, which is AFTER the
14:20->14:35 drop. So the earlier decrement is attributable to run1 (or pdf-extractor growth),
not to run2. Each run appears to hold ~2.5 GiB for its lifetime.

WHY THIS MATTERS TO PO NOW:
1. system-auditor row sys-20260825T142316-4385 ("pdf-extractor memory analysis: genuine working
   set pressure, not leak") is open and routed to po this same tick. Its conclusion looks right,
   but anyone re-reading container_vm_headroom_mb over the next few hours will see a collapsing
   number that is substantially BENCH load, not pdf-extractor. Do not let the bench contaminate
   that investigation's evidence in either direction.
2. Any detector that trips on container_vm_headroom_mb is, right now, primed to fire a false
   positive attributing ad-hoc benchmark load to a long-lived service.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT AT RISK:
  NOT at risk: the gateway. mcp-server sits at 296 MiB against a 3 GiB cap.
  Self-limiting: the bench container is at 99.05% of its OWN 2.5 GiB cap and already UNHEALTHY.
  Per-container caps are containing it as designed — it will OOM itself, not the fleet.
  Genuinely low: VM-wide headroom at 1207 MB. A concurrent run3 alongside a still-live run2
  would be the thing that turns this from contained into an incident.

ROUTER SCOPE: observation only. No spawn, no mutation, no container touched. The bench is a
peer's active experiment and is theirs to stop or let finish.
